div.head: Hl 16.1
div.ab: Gif hit man eft æt þam mæn in Cænt ætfó, þonne tæme he to wic to cyngæs sele to þam mæn ðe him sealde, gif he þane wite ⁊ æt þam teame gebrengen mæge.
Gif hit man eft æt þam mæn in Cænt ætfó, þonne tæme he to wic to cyngæs sele to þam mæn ðe him sealde, gif he þane wite ⁊ æt þam teame gebrengen mæge.
Gif hit man eft æt þam mæn in cænt ætfó, þonne tæme he to wic to cyngæs sele to þam mæn ðe him sealde, gif he þane wite ⁊ æt þam teame gebrengen mæge.

Wenn jemand sie nachher bei jenem Manne in Kent [im Anefang] fasst, dann ziehe dieser [verklagte Käufer die Gewähr] zu [jener] Stadt in Königshalle auf den [Gewährs]mann, der [sie] ihm verkauft hat, wenn er [nämlich] denselben kennt und zu dem Gewährzugsprocesse herbeibringen kann.

If someone afterwards seizes them [by attachment] from that man in Kent, then let this [accused buyer vouch to warranty] at [that] town at the king’s hall upon the [warrantor] who sold [them] to him, if [that is] he knows him and can bring him to the warranty proceedings.

If afterwards it is claimed from the man in Kent, he shall summon as witness, to the king’s residence in London, the man who sold it him, if he knows him and can produce him as warrant for the transaction.

If then it is attached in the possession of the man in Kent, he is to vouch to warranty the man who sold it to him, at the king’s hall in that town, if he knows him and can produce him at that vouching to warranty.

If a person afterwards claim possession of it from that man in Kent, then let him [the person who bought the goods] vouch in the king’s hall in that town that man who sold it to him, if he knows him and is able to bring him to that vouching.

note.seg: London; siehe über solche Abkürzung des Namens Wb: wic
London; on such abbreviation of the name see Wb: wic
Liebermann suggests that London was under the king of Kent when this law was drawn up. We have no evidence elsewhere to this effect. For ætfo see cap. 7 above, and note.

note.label: king’s
note.seg: It is normally assumed that this refers to the Kentish king.

note.label: Kent,
note.seg: In other words, a previous owner or his representative has tracked the purchaser down in Kent to claim that the sale was not legitimate.
